located_point.method: Not located in imagery. Indian Archaeology 1987-88 (PDF page 25, item 35) gives the ancient site, locally known as Bibino Timbo, as 'Lat 22 deg 54' 40" N; Long 70 deg 37' 30" E', 3 km south-east of the present village. That point lies about 0.9 km east of the held 5 km window, which is centred on the village (the site index point). A render of the window's south-east corner shows fields, a canal and a river bend; the fortification could not be recognised.

sources.imagery_result: no lines: the window is centred on the modern village and the printed site coordinate falls just outside it; no Harappan feature was identified

notes: Revision of kuntasi.json, which recorded the town as unmeasurable before we found this plan. Plan only. The plan is a redrawing in a secondary chapter of the plan in Dhavalikar et al. 1996, scanned at about 150 dpi. The inner fortification's east wall, the west wall of the northern room complex and the long wall north of room 24 agree within 2.1 degrees (theta -11.4 to -13.5). The fit on the east wall of the room complex (block-east) wandered across the room interiors in the overlay check and is excluded. The solid part of the outer fortification on the south-east (theta -25.8, under half of its profiles inliers) is not parallel to the inner walls and forms its own system; the drawn outer circuit is irregular.
